content.text: bisphosphonates = the class of choice; zoledronic acid = first-line in professional guidelines; alendronate, risedronate and pamidronate = second-line; zoledronic acid and pamidronate are IV; the others are PO; hypocalcemia after zoledronic acid w 25-OH vitamin D ≤ 10 ng/mL; > 25 ng/mL is suggested. salmon calcitonin = alt if intolerant of or resistant to bisphosphonates.
Zoledronic acid (Reclast) dose, Paget's disease of bone:

Paget's dz: single 5 mg IV infusion. Infusion time ⍉ less than 15 min given over a constant infusion rate. Paget's dz: 1500 mg elemental Ca daily in divided doses (750 mg twice a day, or 500 mg three times a day) and 800 international units vitamin D daily, particularly in the 2 wks after Reclast.

CI: hypocalcemia. CI: CrCl less than 35 mL/min and evidence of acute renal impairment (↑ risk of renal failure). Hypocalcemia may worsen during tx; pts must be adequately supplemented w/ Ca and vitamin D. Renal toxicity: single dose ⍉ exceed 5 mg; infusion ⍉ less than 15 min; risk may be greater w underlying renal impairment or risk factors (advanced age, dehydration); monitor CrCl b4 each dose. ONJ reported; all pts should have a routine oral exam by the prescriber b4 treatment. Atypical fractures incl femoral fractures reported; pts w/ thigh or groin pain should be evaluated to rule out a femoral fracture; re-evaluate risk/benefit and consider interrupting bisphosphonate therapy. Acetaminophen after Reclast may reduce the incidence of acute-phase reaction symptoms. Severe bone, joint, and muscle pain may occur; withhold future doses of Reclast if severe symptoms occur. Loop diuretics: caution due to an ↑ risk of hypocalcemia. Aminoglycosides: caution w/ bisphosphonates incl zoledronic acid (additive effect to lower serum Ca for prolonged periods). OD may cause renal impairment, hypocalcemia, hypophosphatemia, and hypomagnesemia; correct w/ IV calcium gluconate, potassium or sodium phosphate, and magnesium sulfate.
Calcitonin salmon (Miacalcin) dose, Paget's disease of bone:
Symptomatic Paget's dz: 100 USP Units (0.5 mL) per day SC or IM.

CI: hypersensitivity to calcitonin salmon or any of the excipients (reactions incl anaphylaxis w/ death, bronchospasm, and swelling of the tongue or throat). Serious hypersensitivity reactions incl fatal anaphylaxis reported; consider skin testing b4 treatment in pts w/ suspected hypersensitivity to calcitonin salmon. Hypocalcemia w/ tetany (muscle cramps, twitching) and seizure activity reported; hypocalcemia must be corrected b4 initiating therapy. Meta-analysis of 21 trials suggests an ↑ risk of overall malignancies in calcitonin salmon-treated pts. Circulating antibodies to calcitonin salmon may develop and may cause loss of response to treatment. Use for Paget's dz or postmenopausal osteoporosis is recommended w/ an adequate intake of Ca and vitamin D. Concomitant lithium may ↓ plasma lithium concentrations (↑ urinary clearance); lithium dose may require adjustment. OD: hypocalcemic tetany could occur; keep parenteral calcium available for treatment. Most common adverse reactions: nausea w/ or w/o vomiting (10%), injection site inflammation (10%), and flushing of the face or hands (2% to 5%). Due to the possible association between malignancy and calcitonin salmon use, the need for continued therapy should be re-evaluated periodically.
